tagline: Across the Pawcatuck twice, through a mill village.
intro: From Route 2 Shannock Road heads west past marsh and stone-walled fields, crosses the Pawcatuck River into Richmond, and reaches Shannock, a mill village of the nineteenth century. Beyond the second river crossing it is back in Charlestown and runs into woods, curving and dipping under overhanging trees to Route 112. The whole of it is 1.7 miles.
It was one of the first roads named under Rhode Island's scenic roadways program, after neighbors objected to state plans to repave and significantly alter it.

moments.title: Shannock
moments.text: Worker houses from the second half of the 1800s stand close to the road around two mill complexes, with three houses that belonged to the mill owners among them.

moments.title: Horseshoe Falls
moments.text: The 1999 stewardship plan singled out this man-made fall on the Pawcatuck, curved like a horseshoe to turn river water into the mill raceway.

sources.label: RIDOT, Shannock Road Stewardship Plan (1999), pages 1 to 5
